extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants to the Wallace Stegner Fellowship (fiction and poetry writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for applicants to Stanford's two-year Wallace Stegner Fellowship (five fiction and five poetry fellowships per year), describing eligibility, selection criteria, responsibilities, residency, and application logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: In awarding fellowships, we consider the quality of the candidate’s creative work, potential for growth, and ability to contribute to and profit from our writing workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are diverse in style and experience; talent and seriousness are the true common denominators. The program emphasizes both current craft and potential development in a workshop setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: No degree or test requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not require any degrees or tests for admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are evaluated on creative work and potential rather than formal credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum age requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be at least 18 years old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows must be 18 years old when they start the fellowship. Historically accepted fellows have ranged in age from 22 to 75.

rubrics_metrics.name: International applicants welcome / visa handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes. Anyone may apply, regardless of nationality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accepted, international fellows are considered non-matriculated graduate students for visa purposes; the program will work with fellows to obtain a J-1 visa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior publication not required (and can be a mixed signal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior book publication is not required; note that prior publication may suggest a career that has advanced beyond the point when the fellowship’s instruction and workshop critique are most useful in a writer's development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior publication does not disqualify applicants, but it may affect reviewers' judgments about suitability for the program's developmental focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency / local living requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A fellow must live close enough to Stanford in order to attend workshops, readings, and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residency is required so fellows can attend weekly workshops, readings, and lectures; the fellowship is not remote/part-time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time commitment; no concurrent degree programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Stegner Fellowship is a full-time academic commitment and is not intended to be pursued concurrently with another degree program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship is intended to free writers from external full-time obligations so they can focus on their writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation regarding employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Holding a full-time job during the fellowship runs counter to the intention of the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While some fellows may supplement income in the summer, full-time employment during the fellowship is discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop attendance and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows must write and attend a 3-hour weekly workshop; workshops are faculty-led and coincide with Stanford's academic calendar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of the workshop, fellows are expected to actively engage with their cohort's work by reading and thoughtfully commenting on pieces presented. Weekly attendance is a core requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing and revision responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Primarily, Stegner Fellows are required to attend weekly, faculty-led workshops and to write, revise, and then write again, with the goal of a finished manuscript ready for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program frames fellows as working artists whose main responsibility is developing work toward publication-quality manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reading participation
rubrics_metrics.description: During the first year of their fellowship, the fellows participate in the Stegner Fellow Reading series, where they give a public reading of their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are expected to represent their work publicly as part of program activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial support and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The fellowship includes a living stipend of $75,000 per academic year; the program also pays for each fellow’s tuition and health insurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bay Area is expensive; some fellows may need to supplement income (commonly by working during the summer). Teaching appointments to supplement income are sometimes available but not guaranteed, and priority for teaching goes to Ph.D. students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timeline and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Application window: opens on September 1 and closes on November 3 at 11:59 pm PST (November 4 at 2:59 am EST). All applicants are notified of fellowship decisions in April.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are available to all who are interested. For updates, applicants can join the Stegner Fellowship email list or consult the Application FAQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program nature — artist-in-residence, non-degree
rubrics_metrics.description: Though similar in some ways to a MFA program, the fellowship does not offer a degree; we view it as more of an artist-in-residence opportunity for promising writers to spend two years developing their writing in the company of peers and under the guidance of Stanford faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship emphasizes practice and craft over academic credentialing.

rubrics_metrics.name: No favored school/style of writing
rubrics_metrics.description: No school of writing is favored over any other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program values diversity in style and experience; selection and workshop activity are open to varied approaches to craft.
